s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive muscle weakness with respiratory and swallowing difficulties
salient_findings: Progressive muscle weakness starting in lower limbs then upper limbs
High-arched palate, elongated face with dolichocephaly
key_facts: Born at 28 weeks by C-section for fetal distress
Reduced fetal movements and polyhydramnios during antenatal period
Very low birth weight (0.915 kg)
Delayed motor development in early childhood
Wheelchair-bound by age 20
Mildly elevated plasma creatine kinase (379 U/L)
Normal deep tendon reflexes
Normal sensory examination
Normal cerebellar examination
Negative Tensilon test
Generalized cerebral atrophy and dilated ventricles on brain MRI at age 3
Giant motor unit potential and neuropathic changes in proximal and distal muscles on electrophysiological studies
Fatty infiltration, mild fiber size variation, whorled fibers, internalized nuclei on muscle biopsy

shortlist.label: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive muscle weakness with respiratory and swallowing difficulties, mildly elevated plasma creatine kinase, and muscle biopsy findings of fatty infiltration and whorled fibers

shortlist.label: Bethlem myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Delayed motor development, progressive muscle weakness, and muscle biopsy findings of fatty infiltration and whorled fibers

shortlist.label: Collagen VI-related myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive muscle weakness, respiratory difficulties, and muscle biopsy findings of fatty infiltration and whorled fibers

shortlist.label: Rigid spine muscular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive muscle weakness, spinal rigidity, and muscle biopsy findings of fatty infiltration and whorled fibers

shortlist.label: Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Delayed motor development, progressive muscle weakness, and muscle biopsy findings of fatty infiltration and whorled fibers

raw.rationale: The combination of very low birth weight, delayed motor development, progressive muscle weakness, and characteristic muscle biopsy findings such as fatty infiltration, mild fiber size variation, whorled fibers, and internalized nuclei are consistent with Collagen VI-related myopathy. Additionally, the presence of generalized cerebral atrophy and dilated ventricles on brain MRI and the absence of significant family history of neuromuscular disorders also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
rejected.why: Lack of significant family history and absence of typical LGMD muscle biopsy findings

rejected.label: Bethlem myopathy
rejected.why: Typically presents with joint contractures and skin abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Rigid spine muscular dystrophy
rejected.why: Characterized by rigid spine and significant respiratory impairment, which are not the primary features in this case

rejected.label: Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy
rejected.why: Typically presents at birth with severe weakness, contractures, and significant respiratory distress, which is not consistent with the delayed onset of symptoms in this case

gold: SCN4A-associated congenital myopathy with compound heterozygous variants: - c.1841A>T p.(Asn614Ile) - c.4420G>A p.(Ala1474Thr)
